name: Sudan
summary: A devastating civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces has displaced over 10 million people, created the world's largest displacement crisis, and pushed millions to the brink of famine.
context:
Sudan's civil war erupted in April 2023 when tensions between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) escalated into open combat in Khartoum. The conflict quickly spread to Darfur and other regions, reigniting ethnic violence that echoes the genocide of the early 2000s.

The RSF, which evolved from the Janjaweed militia responsible for atrocities in Darfur, has been accused of systematic attacks on civilian populations, particularly targeting non-Arab communities. Reports from the UN and human rights organizations document mass killings, sexual violence, and the deliberate destruction of villages across West Darfur.

The humanitarian toll is staggering. The UN has called Sudan the world's largest displacement crisis, surpassing even Syria and Ukraine. Millions have fled to neighboring Chad, South Sudan, Egypt, and Ethiopia, straining resources in countries already facing their own crises.

Famine conditions have been confirmed in parts of Darfur and Khartoum, with the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) warning that over 25 million people — half the population — face acute hunger. Aid delivery has been severely hampered by active fighting, bureaucratic obstruction, and attacks on humanitarian workers.

Despite the scale of suffering, Sudan's crisis has received a fraction of the international attention and funding directed at other conflicts. Multiple ceasefire attempts have failed, and diplomatic efforts have yet to produce a sustained halt to the violence.

donate.description: Providing shelter, protection, and essential supplies to millions displaced by the conflict inside Sudan and in neighboring countries.

awareness: Follow and share reporting from Sudanese journalists and citizen reporters documenting the conflict — many risk their lives to get the truth out
Share updates from UNHCR, MSF, and OCHA to keep Sudan in the public conversation — coverage has been critically lacking
Organize campus or community screenings of documentaries about Sudan's history and the current crisis
Use #SudanCrisis, #KeepEyesOnSudan, and #SudanWarCrimes on social media to boost visibility and counteract media blackouts
Write op-eds or letters to the editor at your local newspaper calling for more coverage of Sudan
political: Contact your congressional representatives to demand increased humanitarian funding for Sudan and accountability for war crimes
Urge the U.S. State Department to appoint and empower a Special Envoy for Sudan with a clear mandate
Advocate for targeted sanctions against RSF and SAF leaders responsible for atrocities against civilians
Support calls for a UN-mandated arms embargo on all parties to the conflict
Push for the International Criminal Court to investigate and prosecute perpetrators of ethnic violence in Darfur
